item.title: 【DVD】DVD9 - Madonna - The Confessions Tour (DVD-ISO, NTSC, Brazil)
item.description:
I took a look at the Brazilian NTSC version of the Confessions Tour DVD and compared it to the European PAL version. This time, it's kinda tricky. The concert film itself is actually better on the PAL DVD - clearer picture, higher resolution, and more progressive frames. The NTSC version is slightly cropped at the top and bottom, kinda stretched vertically, and a bit more blurry, with significantly more interlacing and movement shadows. This was probably caused by converting the original PAL source to NTSC.

DVD PAL, Europe:

DVD NTSC, Brazil:

DVD PAL, Europe:

DVD NTSC, Brazil:

DVD PAL, Europe:

DVD NTSC, Brazil - movement shadows caused by wrong frame rate:


BUT I can't say that everything is better on the PAL DVD. First of all, the main menu of the disc is kinda stretched horizontally, idk why, whereas the NTSC version contains the disc menu in the correct aspect ratio.

DVD PAL, Europe:

DVD NTSC, Brazil:


The bonus material is also of better quality on the NTSC DVD. It seems like the behind-the-scenes footage was recorded in NTSC, so the PAL DVD now shows movement shadows and more interlaced frames. I also think they may have used different masters here, since the bonus footage on the NTSC DVD has more contrast and shows more of the picture on the right side, whereas the PAL version has a black bar there.

DVD PAL, Europe:

DVD NTSC, Brazil:

DVD PAL, Europe:

DVD NTSC, Brazil:

DVD PAL, Europe:

DVD NTSC, Brazil:


But there is also an one partial exception: the bonus feature "Rollerskating" has the correct frame rate on the NTSC DVD, but the PAL version has a higher video bitrate here. So some details are better to see on the PAL version, but at the same time, some details are lost because of that damn interlacing caused by the wrong frame rate.

So, if you want to watch the tour movie in the best possible quality, I recommend the PAL DVD. And if you want to watch the Confessions Tour backstage footage in the best possible quality, I recommend the NTSC version:

item.title: 【DVD】DVD9 - Madonna - Drowned World Tour 2001 (DVD-ISO, NTSC, Brazil)
item.description:
Let's take a look at the NTSC DVD of the Drowned World Tour 2001 and compare it with the European PAL version. The difference is really remarkable.

First of all, the picture quality on the NTSC version is, once again, noticeably better and sharper than on the PAL version. Secondly, the NTSC version also has significantly more progressive frames, whereas the PAL version often shows those annoying interlaced frames. I have to say, though, that interlacing isn't really a problem in itself, since regular video players can usually deinterlace it. However, I still don't like it, because sometimes you can still see interlacing artifacts. And last but not least, the NTSC version has the correct frame rate, which you can also see when comparing the frames with the PAL version. With the PAL version, two frames are often blended together into a single frame, creating movement shadows. You can clearly see this when looking at the backdrops during Impressive Instant:

I compared the Brazilian DVD with the German Blu-ray release from 2018. Since we're talking about DVD vs. Blu-ray, the Blu-ray is obviously going to be better in terms of picture quality, but I still noticed something interesting. Both versions are cropped differently. The DVD shows more of the picture on the left and at the bottom, but cuts off more of the top and right side. The Blu-ray is the other way around: it shows more of the picture at the top and on the right side, while cropping slightly more from the left and bottom.

Since these are two different releases, they also have different disc menus. And I don't know why, but the "Scene Selection" doesn't work properly on the Brazilian DVD when playing it in VLC, PotPlayer, or MPC-HC. You can't select the next slides (5-8, 9-12, and 13-16), while the rest seems to be functioning normally.
